messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager 11 Elevated tail latency detected on /v1/stream (us-west-2 prod). p95=470ms (norm 120ms), p99=2.6s (norm 340ms), streaming_stalls=29% (5m)
incident-bot: affected pool: gpu-pool-usw2-main; suspect subset of nodes with repeated ECC/AER events and kernel I/O retries

owen: ack. i'm in. pulling router traces and node telemetry. @maya @alex watch customer channels and support, i'll handle infra triage.

maya: on it for comms. alex i'll DM affected account list in a sec. any clue regional failover needed?

owen: quick metric: 
```
metrics.query("sum(streaming_stalls{route='/v1/stream',region='us-west-2'}[10m])")
```
nowen: returns ~410 stalls in 10m, ~11 customers with >4 stalls, 3 customers with 504/timeout spikes.

rachel: pulling dmesg from gpu-node-88 (one noisy node):
```
[543210.001] thermal: fan_ctrl: lost heartbeat on fan 2
[543210.005] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5c:00): 45, pid=33421, CE error, recovery performed
[543216.789] kernel: pcieport 0000:5c:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received
[543217.340] nvme0n1: I/O 99887 aborted, status: timeout
```

priya: Xid 45 + fan heartbeat loss + AER uncorrected = classic flaky PCIe riser or fan controller path leading to stalls and occasional device timeouts. could also be a riser cable seat issue.

nowen: plan: isolate node-88 and node-91 (same rack). cordon + drain, route new streaming sessions to us-west-2-fallback-quantized and warm model caches. consider cross-region soft-failover to us-east-1 for critical customers if p99 stays >1s.

infra-bot: Action: cordon nodes=[gpu-node-88,gpu-node-91] reason="AER/Xid45/fan-heartbeat loss" initiated_by=owen
infra-bot: Routing change: prefer pool=gpu-pool-usw2-fallback-quantized, fallback warmup started

alex: drafting customer note: "We routed traffic to fallback capacity in us-west-2 after detecting GPU hardware issues affecting streaming latency. We're draining affected nodes and replacing hardware. Some customers may see transient retries; we're contacting impacted accounts." send?

maya: send now, include that we're applying server-side graceful-retry (2 attempts) for stalled streams and avoid hard 504s.

nowen: injecting router policy snippet: 
```
route.rules.stream_on_stall = {action: retry_with_reconnect, max_retries:2, backoff: 1500ms, on_fail: failover_to_fallback}
```

priya: synthetic checks on fallback look reasonable: p95 ~210ms, p99 ~720ms (warming), stall_rate dropped to ~6% for new sessions. existing stuck streams still present; planning forced-cancel + client-reconnect header.

ops: caution 1 if we flood clients with reconnects we could get a reconnect storm. suggest staggered reconnect header like X-RW-Reconnect-Delay: randomized 1-4s.

nowen: applied staggered reconnect. infra-bot: autoscaler bump +4 fallback nodes.

rachel: HW ticket HW-4601 opened: "gpu-node-88/91 AER/Xid45 + fan-heartbeat loss; suspect riser/fan-controller. Request DC swap and PCIe riser inspection." assigned to @hw-bot.

infra-bot: Drain progress: node=gpu-node-88 migrated_sessions=421 active_streams_forced_retry=27
infra-bot: Drain progress: node=gpu-node-91 migrated_sessions=398 active_streams_forced_retry=31

nowen: after partial reroute p95 down to 160ms within 7m; p99 still ~980ms but trending down. streaming_stalls now 4.8% (5m).

alex: customer comms sent to top-3 affected accounts; support triaging one account that saw multiple 504s. no escalations so far.

priya: noticed an oddity: when streams were moved to quantized fallback, a small subset of sessions experienced duplicated tokens on reconnect because client SDK retried without idempotency key. we flagged SDK team.

maya: noted. add that to postmortem action: enforce idempotency/reconnect semantics in SDK for streaming reconnection to avoid duplicates.

rachel: DC notes: out-of-band BMC logs show intermittent PCIe link resets at the riser slot; they recommend full riser reseat and fan controller firmware dump. scheduling on-site swap.

hw-bot: DC scheduled physical intervention in 2 hours PT. requested to keep nodes offline until replacement completes.

infra-bot: drain complete: gpu-node-88 migrated_sessions=438 gpu-node-91 migrated_sessions=410 total_forced_retries=58

nowen: handover/rotation: i'm off in 12m. @maya can you take primary after I rotate? watch p99 and streaming_stall_rate <5% target. Also track SDK idempotency issue.

maya: taking over. summary for handoff:
- cause: hardware path degradation (AER/Xid45 + fan heartbeat loss) likely riser/fan-controller leading to NVMe I/O timeouts and GPU hangs
- mitigation: cordon+drain nodes 88/91, reroute to quantized fallback, autoscaler +4 fallback nodes, injected staggered reconnect & retry policy
- customer impact: ~11 customers with degraded streams, 3 with timeouts; top 3 notified
- next steps: HW-4601 physical swap, postmortem, SDK reconnect/idempotency fix, add PCIe AER + fan-heartbeat to auto-evict rules

priya: metrics update at handoff: p95=150ms, p99=405ms, streaming_stall_rate=3.9% (5m). good progress.

alex: customers acknowledged the update, support opened tickets for the 3 timed-out accounts.

ops: action item: add riser-slot AER counts and fan-heartbeat loss as early-warning metrics. putting on infra backlog.

rachel: marking nodes DO NOT REINTRODUCE until DC validates full pass on post-swap tests. HW-4601 updated.

infra-bot: incident mitigated. Postmortem required (customer-impact >10 accounts). Postmortem link: https://redwood/incidents/HW-4601

maya: closing thread and linking postmortem draft to ticket when available. :white_check_mark:
